claims.text: An ultra-dense, continuous, low-porosity boride barrier produced by optimized powder-pack boriding will significantly improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
Conventional powder-pack boriding produces a more porous and discontinuous boride layer than the proposed optimized treatment.
Boriding temperature and duration affect growth and thickness of the boride layer.
Adjustment of boriding temperature and duration can produce an ultra-dense, continuous boride layer.
Adjustment of the ambient atmosphere during powder-pack boriding helps produce an ultra-dense, continuous boride layer.
Approximately 660 °C represents a relevant molten-aluminum exposure temperature for industrial hot-dip aluminum plating.
A low-porosity, adherent boride layer minimizes pathways for molten aluminum to enter the substrate.
A denser boride layer reduces diffusion of aluminum into the substrate.
A denser boride layer limits reaction sites available for molten-aluminum attack.
Reduced aluminum diffusion and fewer reaction sites decrease the molten-aluminum corrosion rate.
Powder-pack boriding can substantially increase the surface hardness of CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy.
Powder-pack boriding improves the wear behavior of CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy, including by lowering its friction coefficient.
The observed hardness and wear improvements suggest that an optimized boride layer will also resist molten-aluminum corrosion.
The optimized treatment will produce a statistically significant reduction in weight loss relative to conventional boriding during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure.
The optimized treatment will produce a statistically significant reduction in aluminum penetration depth relative to conventional boriding.
The corrosion-resistance improvement will persist during continuous molten-aluminum exposure near 660 °C for durations typical of hot-dip plating.
The protective effect may diminish when exposure temperature or duration exceeds the design specifications of the optimized boride layer.
The magnitude of the corrosion improvement may depend on variations in boriding parameters and service conditions.
